briefdescription.para: Constructs an SDep with the specified values.
Returns true if the specified SDep is equivalent except for latency.
Returns the latency value for this edge, which roughly means the minimum number of cycles that must elapse between the predecessor and the successor, given that they have this edge between them.
Sets the latency for this edge.
Returns an enum value representing the kind of the dependence.
Shorthand for getKind() != SDep::Data.
Tests if this is an Order dependence between two memory accesses where both sides of the dependence access memory in non-volatile and fully modeled ways.
Tests if this is an Order dependence that is marked as a barrier.
Tests if this is could be any kind of memory dependence.
Tests if this is an Order dependence that is marked as "must alias", meaning that the SUnits at either end of the edge have a memory dependence on a known memory location.
Tests if this a weak dependence.

detaileddescription.para: Weak dependencies are considered DAG edges for height computation and other heuristics, but do not force ordering. Breaking a weak edge may require the scheduler to compensate, for example by inserting a copy.

briefdescription.para: Tests if this is an Order dependence that is marked as "artificial", meaning it isn't necessary for correctness.
Tests if this is an Order dependence that is marked as "cluster", meaning it is artificial and wants to be adjacent.
Tests if this is a Data dependence that is associated with a register.
Returns the register associated with this edge.

detaileddescription.para: This is only valid on Data, Anti, and Output edges. On Data edges, this value may be zero, meaning there is no associated register.

briefdescription.para: Assigns the associated register for this edge.

detaileddescription.para: This is only valid on Data, Anti, and Output edges. On Anti and Output edges, this value must not be zero. On Data edges, the value may be zero, which would mean that no specific register is associated with this edge.
